description: Composite figure (4x2 grid of image pairs) comparing raw micrographs with MatSAM segmentation masks for eight microstructures. Column headers read "Raw image" and "MatSAM"; the left block is polycrystalline, the right block multiphase. (a) PI-1: equiaxed grains with thin dark etched boundaries and scattered small black particles; MatSAM output is a black field with white cell-like boundary lines. (b) HEA: coarse grains with faint, locally invisible boundaries; (c) SS: equiaxed grains; (d) PI-2: the only colour micrograph, with blue/yellow tinted grains (polarised-light look); in all four MatSAM draws continuous white boundaries. (e) DP590-2: bright irregular elongated islands in a darker matrix; (f) DP590-1: blurred grey islands in dark matrix; (g) NBS-1: one large bright region plus fine dots; (h) UHCS: dark matrix densely filled with small bright spheroidal particles; MatSAM outputs are white filled blobs matching these constituents. Paired coloured arrows (orange, yellow, cyan/blue) point to the same locations in raw and mask; in (a) a cyan arrow marks a small dark particle and orange arrows mark boundary junctions. No scale bars, axes or printed numbers appear. The figure argues MatSAM recovers missing/non-closing grain boundaries and separates multiphase constituents without training.

subfigures.description: Raw image labelled a: PI-1 polycrystalline optical micrograph with equiaxed grains, thin dark etched boundaries and small black particles. MatSAM panel shows the same field as a binary mask: black background with white grain-boundary network. Three coloured arrows (orange, yellow, cyan) mark a boundary junction, a boundary segment and a small dark particle in both raw and mask.

Raw image labelled b: HEA, coarse-grained structure with few, faint and locally discontinuous boundaries. MatSAM mask reproduces the grain network with white continuous boundaries; orange arrow at left and yellow arrow at lower right.

Raw image labelled c: SS, equiaxed grained grayscale micrograph with moderately fine, wavy boundaries. MatSAM mask gives the corresponding white boundary network; orange arrow upper-left, yellow arrow lower-left.

Raw image labelled d: PI-2, the only colour micrograph (blue- and yellow-tinted grains, polarised-light appearance) with irregular grain boundaries. MatSAM mask shows continuous white boundaries; orange, cyan and yellow arrows in raw and mask.

Raw image labelled e: DP590-2, bright irregular, elongated/blocky islands in a darker matrix (scratch-like surface features visible). MatSAM mask renders those islands as white filled blobs on black; orange arrow marks one island.
Raw image labelled f: DP590-1, blurred grayscale image with grey blocky/elongated islands in a darker matrix. MatSAM mask extracts them as white blobs on black. No arrows visible.

Raw image labelled g: NBS-1, grayscale field with one large bright rounded region and numerous fine bright dots in the matrix. MatSAM mask gives a large white blob plus small white dots; orange, cyan and yellow arrows mark selected features.
Raw image labelled h: UHCS, dark matrix with thin dark grain boundaries and dense small bright spheroidal particles. MatSAM mask shows the particles as small white dots on black. No arrows visible.

observations.observation: The figure is a 4x2 arrangement of image pairs, each pair being a raw micrograph (left) and its MatSAM segmentation (right), with column headers 'Raw image' and 'MatSAM'.
Small white-on-black letter labels a, b, c, d (left block) and e, f, g, h (right block) are printed in the top-left corner of each raw image.
The caption states the left block shows polycrystalline images and the right block shows multiphase images.
The caption names the samples: (a) PI-1, (b) HEA, (c) SS, (d) PI-2, (e) DP590-2, (f) DP590-1, (g) NBS-1, and (h) UHCS.
The caption states that arrows point to noteworthy areas and that a pair of arrows shares the same colour, i.e. arrows link the same location in a raw image and its MatSAM output.

MatSAM outputs in panels (a)-(d) are binary images consisting of a black background with white lines tracing grain boundaries; outputs in (e)-(h) are black backgrounds with white filled blobs representing the second phase/particles.
Panel (a) raw image contains small black dots (particles/inclusions) inside the light grains, and a cyan-coloured arrow points to one such dot in both the raw image and the MatSAM mask.
Panel (h) UHCS raw image shows a dark matrix with thin dark grain boundaries and a dense population of small bright spheroidal particles, which the MatSAM mask renders as discrete small white dots.
Panel (e) DP590-2 raw image shows bright irregular elongated islands in a darker matrix, extracted as white blobs by MatSAM.
Panel (d) is the only coloured raw micrograph in the group, with grains tinted blue and yellow, whereas all other raw panels are grayscale.
No scale bars, magnification values, axes, legends or printed numeric values are visible in any panel.

The citing text states that incompleteness or non-closing of grain boundaries, often from uneven or incomplete etching, is the common issue in these images and causes under-segmentation in untailored approaches.
The citing text states that in (b) the grain boundaries in the region indicated by the arrow are nearly invisible, yet MatSAM can still infer the missing parts.
The citing text states that in (d) some boundaries are hard to tell at the grain interfaces, but MatSAM captures and reasonably recognizes the subtle changes near the boundaries.

The citing text states that MatSAM consistently provided reasonable outputs even for complex, variable and difficult-to-interpret micrographs, illustrated through these polycrystalline and multiphase examples.

unreadable_items: No scale bars or magnification values are printed in any panel, so the physical field of view of every micrograph is unknown.
Panel (h): the small bright carbide/particle features are near the resolution limit, so their individual sizes cannot be measured.
Panel (f): the raw image is visibly blurred and partially out of focus, so the exact phase shapes cannot be traced by eye.
The modality per panel (optical vs SEM/BSE) is not stated anywhere in the figure; only (a) and (d) show colour that indicates optical metallography, while (e)-(h) are grayscale and could be either.
